_README: Wiki-sourced corrections to a gear-planner affix NAME (#227). Global, not per-item: every occurrence of source_name becomes canonical_name. Applied by src/name_corrections.py BEFORE variant expansion and BEFORE rankable_affixes(), so one corrected affix block flows into verify/coverage, the picker vocabulary, the solver, browse, and the exports from one place. gear-planner remains the sole authority for WHICH affixes an item has; the wiki is the authority for what the enchantment is CALLED. Pair every entry with an affix_aliases.json entry mapping source_name -> canonical_name, so a player typing the gear-planner name still resolves.
_guards: The build FAILS when source_name is no longer present upstream (the rename has become a silent no-op) or when canonical_name is ALREADY a native gear-planner name (renaming onto it would merge two affixes upstream keeps distinct). A correction file that cannot go stale unnoticed is the only kind worth having.
_precedent: Movement Speed, Physical Sheltering, and Armor-Piercing are all native pipeline-minted names with the spoken variant (Striding, PRR, Fortification Bypass) aliased on top. An alias alone cannot do this job: the picker canonicalizes typed input, but the solver matches item affixes by name, so a canonical name no item carries scores zero.

corrections.evidence: The Enhancements list on Item:Legendary_Icewalkers renders 'Enhanced Ki'; the Enhanced Ki page describes it as increasing the rate at which the user gains ki with each successful attack. gear-planner stores the same enchantment as bare 'Ki' with a magnitude and no type.
corrections.reason: Reported by a player who could not find 'enhanced ki' in the priority picker. The stored name is a shortening, not a different enchantment: 19 worn variants across 5 slots carry values 1-5, matching the wiki's per-item values.
corrections.note: This affix is untyped upstream, so it is ALSO gated by data/seed/compendium/untyped_rankable.json. Renaming it does not by itself make it rankable.
corrections.channel: all channels. Inert until the 2026-08-18 refresh, which re-encoded the type field: `Ki` went from untyped (invisible to iter_affixes, #229's mask) to 20 gate-visible records typed `Untyped`, arming this entry.

all channels. Was augment-pool-only pre-refresh (two Solar Gem of Enduring stones); the 2026-08-18 refresh moved upstream to `False Life (%)` wholesale — 34 items / 2 crafting / 4 sets — while `Legendary Conditioning` left raw entirely, which is what arms this entry.
corrections.evidence: #376 — one mechanic stored under two names, so the two sat in separate buckets and SUMMED. ddowiki Conditioning: "This enchantment gives a +X% Legendary bonus to Maximum Hit points". Our only two False Life (%) carriers are the Solar Gem of Enduring pair, listed on Lunar_and_Solar_Gems as "Enduring - Legendary Bonus to Maximum Hit Points". Same mechanic, same bonus type, so they must share a bucket and take the highest: Baphomet's Reign 15% + Solar Gem 10% reported 25% where the game gives 15%. Flat False Life is a DIFFERENT enchantment (no percentage variant; Vitality/Profane/Insight/Enhancement/Quality across 510 items) and is untouched. No item carries both names.

corrections.evidence: https://ddowiki.com/page/Unconscious section 'Extending unconsciousness range' lists all sources together as enhancement bonuses to one range: 'Holding On: +40 enhancement bonus', 'Undying: enhancement bonus scaling with level', 'Undying Sapphire: +65 / +225 enhancement bonus', 'Weighty Asset: +100 enhancement bonus'. `Incapacitation range` (which the Undying enchantment links) REDIRECTS to that same page, so the two spellings are one mechanic. Harvested 2026-08-30.
corrections.note: #649 — REVERSES the #632 note that used to sit here, which declined the rename of `Undying` because "moving it would change a stat name in saved builds to fix 3 records". Two things changed. The stat-name objection is answered by the alias in affix_aliases.json: `Undying` resolves to this canonical, so a saved build that ranked it keeps scoring and nothing a player stored is lost. And the cost was never 3 records — it was that `Undying` names ONE of the four enchantments feeding the stat, so the priority list read 'Undying 225' while the item said 'Weighty Asset', and the maintainer asked what the two had to do with each other. That is the confusion a canonical named after one of its members produces. `Unconsciousness Range` is the wiki's own phrase for the mechanic ('Extending unconsciousness range') and is a member of none of them, so it cannot mislead the same way. The engraved name still rides on `via`, so every card reads what the item actually says.
corrections.canon_defense_note: ARMED by the 397c673 (2026-09-23) refresh. Upstream carried 'Unconsciousness Range' natively in its crafting dump (3 occurrences at 767a7f7) and now carries it nowhere, while still emitting all three variants. The rename therefore stopped being a tidy-up and became load-bearing: without it our canonical has no native source and the stat imports under upstream's spellings, scoring zero for a player who ranked it. `merge_into_existing` is kept and is currently inert — it re-applies the moment upstream reintroduces the canonical.

corrections.evidence: https://ddowiki.com/page/Mind_Drain states the effect outright and lists exactly our four carriers: 'This item reduces your maximum spell points by 5% while worn. Found on: (4) Mind Drain items: Baphomet's Reign, Clouded Dreams, Legendary Lucid Dreams, Lucid Dreams.' Unconditional while worn. A percent of max SP, so it belongs to the percent stat, not the flat one — flat and percent are deliberately distinct stats (tests/test_vocabulary.py::test_unit_marker_is_significant_flat_vs_percent_distinct). Harvested 2026-08-30.
corrections.note: #639 — `Mind Drain` is not a stat; the spell-point pool it drains is. Merged so the penalty lands in Maximum Spell Points (%), with the engraved name kept on `via`.

corrections.evidence: https://ddowiki.com/page/Power_Drain is a DISAMBIGUATION page with two readings, and the distinction matters: 'Power Drain (clicky) found on Vile Blasphemy, an effect regenerates SP over time' versus 'Power Drain (enchantment) found on Infused Chaosrobe and such, penalize your maximum SP'. All four of our carriers are the enchantment reading and the enchantment page lists exactly them. It states a SUSTAINED value — 'You lose 30 maximum spell points' — so by conditional_affix_quarantine's own discipline this is a value correction rather than a quarantine. Two conditionals are disclosed rather than modelled: up to 60 for Sorcerer and Favored Soul (we carry no class model), and suppression while wearing a Sustaining Symbiont. Harvested 2026-08-30.
corrections.note: #639 — `Power Drain` is not a stat; the spell-point pool it drains is. Merged so the penalty lands in Wizardry, with the engraved name kept on `via`.

corrections.channel: crafting/augment pool - the three Solar Gems are the only carriers of the source name. The sets channel already emits the canonical, across both set containers, which is the whole point of the fold.
corrections.evidence: #672 - one enchantment stored under two names, in separate buckets. ddowiki Lunar_and_Solar_Gems states the Solar Gem's effect as a "Legendary Bonus to Spell Critical Damage" at +5/+10/+15 for ML1/ML20/ML30. gear-planner attaches the affix name `Spell Intensity` to items titled exactly `Solar Gem of Spell Critical Damage (Heroic|Epic|Legendary)`, type Legendary, values 5/10/15 - the same ladder on the same three named objects. Eight distinct sets across BOTH set containers - membership_set_defs (Delight of the Devourer, Vol's Influence, both Legendary variants, Deacon of the Auricular Sacrarium) and the per-item parsed_set_bonuses copy (Deacon again plus the Elder's Knowledge chain: Elder's / Epic / Legendary at 5/10/15) - already carry `Spell Critical Damage` at bonus type Legendary, wiki-sourced raw text "+15 Legendary bonus to Spell Critical Damage". Same bonus type on both sides, so the same page's stacking rule makes summing wrong: they must share a bucket and take the max. The population closes - `Spell Intensity` has exactly three carriers in the built dataset and all three are those gems, so no occurrence of the name means anything else. Measured 2026-09-02 on a dataset rebuilt from 24647e4.
corrections.reason: #672 - the DDO wiki is this repo's authority for what an enchantment is CALLED, and it calls this Spell Critical Damage; `Spell Intensity` is gear-planner's spelling and appears in no wiki sentence about these gems. Minting the wiki name also aligns the picker with the augment a player is looking at: the gem is literally titled `Solar Gem of Spell Critical Damage`, which is the confusion #404's companion hint was built to paper over. The paired affix_aliases.json entry keeps a typed or saved `Spell Intensity` resolving.

corrections.channel: sets only — the plural exists nowhere else in the corpus, so the items, crafting and augment channels are EXPECTED per-channel misses (#376).
corrections.evidence: ddowiki `Resistance (enchantment)` states one enchantment here and gives it in the singular: "In addition to the universal Resistance bonuses to saves ... specialized item enchantments exist that affect only a subset of saving throws: ... Spell saves ('Realistic' prefix) - provide Resistance bonuses against spells from all schools of magic". `Spell Save` REDIRECTS to that page, so the wiki names the singular as the title for this mechanic. Measured 2026-09-18 against the pinned snapshot: the plural occurs 4 times in the whole corpus, all of them inside the two `Slave's Endurance` set tiers, and ZERO items or crafting options carry it; the singular is on 93 item affixes (Resistance 72, Insight 18, Quality 2, Enhancement 1). No record carries both spellings, so this is one mechanic under two spellings and not a merge of two (the same-item co-occurrence rule). The canonical is absent from the sets channel, so nothing is collapsed.
corrections.reason: #769 — the set channel's spelling of the enchantment the item channel calls `Spell Save`. Surfaced the moment the Slaver's Set Bonus pool stopped dropping `Slave's Endurance`: that set was the plural's only carrier, so admitting the set made the plural rankable for the first time and the umbrella detector flagged it as an unadjudicated candidate. It needs no adjudication entry — `Spell Save` already carries one (atomic, harvested 2026-08-13) and this rename resolves the plural into it, which is what the detector's closed vocabulary asks for. Without the rename the set's headline defensive affix would score zero for every player who ranked the name 93 items engrave.

corrections.evidence: Both wiki pages define the SAME mechanic — an Enhancement-typed percentage discount to spell point cost. https://ddowiki.com/page/Power_Store: 'All spells cast while holding this item receive an enhancement bonus of -10% spell point cost.' https://ddowiki.com/page/Magical_Efficiency: 'You take a X% Enhancement discount to the Spell Point cost of your spells', with named 5% and 10% variants. Power Store is the engraved item-side name for the 10% variant.
corrections.reason: #619 regression guard. Upstream itself folded 'Power Store' into 'Magical Efficiency' up to commit 767a7f7 and DROPPED the fold at 397c673, moving 8 item records and 1 crafting option onto a standalone 'Power Store' name. Bucket keys are stat||type, so leaving the two apart puts one game mechanic in two buckets that SUM — the #632/#376 failure. Restoring the fold as our canon also keeps the eight #619 value corrections on target.
corrections.channel: all channels. Item roster (8 records: the five Cormyrian Green Dragon bodies, both Green Dragonscale Bracers, Staff of the Petitioner) and the crafting catalog (Facet of Condensed Power, Green Augment Slot).
corrections.not_a_canon_defense: Deliberately NOT canon_defense: upstream still emits our canonical 'Magical Efficiency' (99 item / 6 crafting records), so the canon is not at risk and the KTD3 guard would rightly call a declared defence inert. This entry exists to MERGE upstream's re-split name back into the one bucket the mechanic belongs in.

corrections.evidence: The engraved name states its own stat: 'Inherent Acid Resistance - 5: This item provides a +5 Insight bonus to your Acid Resistance'. It is the SAME stat as 'Acid Resistance', not a sibling of it — the wiki sentence names that stat outright. Read on the rendered item pages carrying the heroic version (The Pea Shooter / Hand of the Tombs / Chill of Winter / Arcing Sky) on 2026-09-22.
corrections.reason: New at the 397c673 refresh: upstream's T2/T3 (Equipment) crafting pools now carry the engraved label with the magnitude stripped off the end, leaving a trailing ' -' in the name (Insight 25 at T2, Competence 17 at T3). Bucket keys are stat||type, so an item carrying a native 'Acid Resistance' AND this crafted option under a different name puts one stat in two buckets that SUM where the game takes the max — the #632 defect. Folding also keeps these options visible to a player who ranked the plain stat.
corrections.channel: crafting catalog only (T2/T3 Equipment pools); absent from the item roster.

_pending: #374/U2 — an entry may carry pending_upstream + pending_reason when it is declared one unit AHEAD of the refreshed gear-planner snapshot that arms it. Pending entries are exempt from assert_all_reached (they reach nothing by construction) and excluded from the KTD3 declared-live set. The exemption is self-retiring: assert_canon_defense fails the build the moment the raw data arms an entry whose marker is still set.
_canon_defense: #374/KTD3 — canon_defense marks an entry that defends one of OUR enchantment names against an upstream vocabulary flip. src/name_corrections.assert_canon_defense compares the live (non-pending) canon_defense set against vocabulary.armed_canon_variants(), derived from the raw snapshot by the direct Rule A predicate, and fails in EITHER direction. Never hand-list the armed set: a hand-list is right once and rots at the next refresh, silently.
